transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-05-03
Start time (UTC): 2027-05-03T16:30:00Z
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Park (Redwood AE); Marco Santini (Redwood SE); Rebecca Lin (Helios Head of MLOps); Jordan Miles (Helios Platform Eng); Samir Patel (Helios SRE)

Auto-summary: Quick console walkthrough focused on tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Customer wants to understand how to debug token-level latency spikes, PII redaction, and how request logs correlate to traces for regulatory audits. Plan: Redwood to send security pack and run a small pilot with sample failing prompt.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alyssa Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alyssa, AE at Redwood. With me is Marco our SE who will walk through the Console tracing and request logs.
[00:18] Marco Santini: Hi team, great to meet you. I'll share my screen - I'm on the console demo tenant. We'll start with the tracing tab which shows per-request timelines, operator events, kernel selection points, cache hits and misses, and the downstream model time.
[00:35] Rebecca Lin: Awesome. Our use-case is health-chatbot, lots of PII concerns, occasional hallucinations, and sporadic latency spikes - we want to root-cause whether it's model, infra, or prompt.
[00:47] Jordan Miles: Also curious about retention for request logs and whether we can export logs for audits.
[00:52] Marco Santini: Totally. So in the tracing view you can search by request id, correlation id, or user id. Each trace has a waterfall: routing -> batching -> model inference -> post-processing. You'll see things like "KV cache hit" (sometimes transcribed as K-V cash), and if there's a cache miss it'll show the fill duration.
[01:15] Marco Santini: I'll pull up an example. Here's a request that had a 2.4s tail - you can see the timeline spike inside the tokenizer step and then a long model step. If you click into the model step we surface kernel selection (e.g., fp16 kernel vs quantized kernel), GPU scheduling delays, and whether the request was routed to a fallback model.
[01:40] Samir Patel: Can you filter traces by model variant? We often A/B with a quantized 8-bit model and a full fp16 model.
[01:46] Marco Santini: Yes, filter by model name, variant, and even by hardware tier. You can also group traces by model variant to see distribution of latency and error rates.
[02:02] Marco Santini: Next, the error analysis view aggregates errors across requests: decoding failures, generation length truncations, hallucination flags (from our eval hooks), and user-reported issues. We cluster similar traces and show representative examples.
[02:18] Rebecca Lin: How do you detect hallucinations? We have sensitive PHI and need high precision.
[02:23] Marco Santini: We run model-output checks and heuristics, plus you can plug in your own evals. The console surfaces a confidence and a pattern match for hallucination heuristics; it's not perfect but it's useful to prioritize. We also integrate regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[02:42] Jordan Miles: On retention - what's stored in request logs by default? We can't keep raw PHI longer than 30 days.
[02:49] Alyssa Park: Good question. By default hosted logs keep full request/response for 7 days, request metadata for 30 days. For Dedicated or Private we offer configurable retention and can integrate with your KMS for encrypted-at-rest logs; you can also enable PII redaction to strip or mask tokens before storage.
[03:05] Rebecca Lin: Can we export logs for audits if we need to hand them off to compliance?
[03:09] Marco Santini: Yes - export bundle includes trace JSON, raw request/response (unless redaction enabled) and token-level timing. We can also provide signed audit logs for retention compliance. We'll attach a sample export after the call.
[03:26] Jordan Miles: You mentioned token-level timing. Can we see per-token latency and token cost breakdown?
[03:31] Marco Santini: Yep. The request log has per-token timestamps, per-token compute time, and a cost estimate. There's also a timeline heatmap for long-running generations so you can spot whether the encoder or decoder is the hotspot.
[03:47] Samir Patel: In our system, intermittent slowdowns correlate with spikes in incoming concurrent queries - is there a way to see batching behaviour?
[03:55] Marco Santini: In the trace you can see batching windows and batch sizes. We show the queue wait time and the batch composition - sometimes a long-tail batch can add 200-300ms to a request. We also show autoscale events if you're on Dedicated.
[04:12] Rebecca Lin: From a security perspective, we need SSO (SAML), RBAC, and audit trails for who re-ran a request. Are those visible?
[04:20] Alyssa Park: Yes. Console has RBAC roles, SAML SSO, and per-action audit logs. The request history shows replays and who replayed.
[04:28] Marco Santini: I'm going to recreate a failing trace. Here's the sample prompt Rebecca provided earlier - thank you - I'll run it in the debugger.
[04:36] Marco Santini: You can see the raw request on the right; there's a highlight where the decoder emits an unexpected token sequence. The error analysis flagged it as a decoding failure, and recommended prompt adjustments and a model variant suggestion (lower temperature, or try the non-quantized variant).
[04:55] Rebecca Lin: Do you have a way to automatically retry on decode failures with a fallback model? That would be helpful.
[05:00] Marco Santini: Yes, rollout policies support automatic fallback to a compatible variant - you can set thresholds for retries and increase determinism on retry. We'll show policy config later.
[05:10] Jordan Miles: How intrusive is redaction? If we enable token masking, can we still do debugging?
[05:16] Marco Santini: Redaction masks sensitive tokens in stored logs but you can configure that certain roles (with higher privileges and key access) can request a decrypted view - this is gated by KMS and audit logs. For pilot we can provide a redacted export and a masked-plus-decryption example under NDA.
[05:35] Samir Patel: What's the overhead of tracing on latency? Do traces add measurable overhead?
[05:40] Marco Santini: Tracing is asynchronous for the heavy payloads. We sample full request storage by default, with lightweight event streaming for every request. There is minimal overhead in the hot path - typical <5ms - but full token-level serialization is done off the critical path.
[05:56] Alyssa Park: Quick note on compliance: for Dedicated/Private deployments we can ship a customer-managed control plane or VPC peering; logs can stay in your account under your retention policy.
[06:07] Rebecca Lin: For the pilot, we likely want Dedicated and to run a three-week soak test with our traffic. Can you provision an 8-GPU cluster and give us expected throughput numbers?
[06:16] Marco Santini: Yes - for an 8xA100 setup with 2k tokens average per request we estimate ~120 req/s with batching optimizations. We'll include conservative latency percentiles and cost estimates in the follow-up.
[06:30] Jordan Miles: Are there any known Gotchas with private network MTUs or cert rotation that bite customers?
[06:36] Marco Santini: Cert rotation is automatic for hosted; for Private we give a rotation guide. MTU problems show up rarely - we recommend standard 1500 and avoid jumbo frames on the path to GPU hosts. We'll include a network checklist.
[06:52] Marco Santini: Back to the console - here's the request-log view showing raw payload, token-level timing, and the ability to re-run the request from the same panel. You can toggle to see the policy decisions that happened during routing (why a request hit the cheaper fallback model).
[07:12] Samir Patel: Re-run - does that count against usage? We need to avoid double billing when debugging.
[07:17] Alyssa Park: Replays for debugging can be flagged and excluded from billing in Dedicated/pilot accounts; for hosted we'd normally bill, but in pilots we can arrange credits.
[07:28] Rebecca Lin: On the error clustering: are clusters stable over time or do they drift with model updates?
[07:34] Marco Santini: They can drift - that's why we tie regression alerts to prompt sets. When you deploy a new model we run a smoke evaluation on your control prompts and surface regressions with example traces.
[07:47] Jordan Miles: Can we integrate our existing observability stack (we use Datadog) for alerts?
[07:52] Marco Santini: Yes, we have webhooks and a Datadog integration to forward summaries and alerts. Full trace exports can also be pushed to your storage.
[08:01] Rebecca Lin: Example: we had a case where a specific user_id triggered a big spike - can we search by user and see all requests chained by correlation id?
[08:09] Marco Santini: Yes. Correlation search is first-class - you can visualize a session timeline and see downstream calls and retries.
[08:18] Samir Patel: For the pilot, we'll want to stress the system with concurrent spike tests. Can you help define the load test script?
[08:24] Alyssa Park: Absolutely. Marco's team can help with a load script and we'll run a joint test.
[08:29] Marco Santini: I'll capture the sample errors and attach the trace bundle to the deal. Also I'll include a short how-to doc for reading the trace waterfall and a checklist for investigating latency spikes.
[08:40] Rebecca Lin: Great. One last question: can we redact user identifiers but still search by hashed id?
[08:46] Marco Santini: Yes - we support hashing or tokenization at ingestion so you can keep searchable keys without storing raw PII.
[08:53] Alyssa Park: Ok let's recap next steps.
[08:56] Alyssa Park: Reed - sorry Rebecca - we'll send SOC2/ISO docs, network checklist, and sample trace export. Marco will run the export and attach it to the CRM and propose dates for a pilot on May 12. Rebecca to share the failing prompt and an example trace id.
[09:12] Rebecca Lin: I'll share the prompt and trace id by EOD Monday.
[09:15] Jordan Miles: Thanks, this was helpful.
[09:17] Marco Santini: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the bundle.
[09:20] Alyssa Park: Thanks all - end call.

Call wrap / Notes:
- Pilot interest: Dedicated 8-GPU cluster, three-week soak.
- Security asks: SOC2/ISO, SAML, KMS integration, PII redaction.
- Technical asks: per-token timing, batching visibility, error clustering, exportable trace bundles.

End of transcript.
